subject.title: Water Replenishment District of Southern California Board, Division 4

text: In 2022, the voters honored me by electing me as their public servant and Director of the Water Replenishment District of Southern California, Division 4. Since taking office, I have worked to protect our groundwater by keeping it safe, sustainable, and affordable. Today, groundwater remains the most affordable water supply in SoCal.
As a teacher, healthcare professional, and lifelong resident who lives and works within Division 4, I understand our communities' needs firsthand.

In 2026, I was unanimously appointed Board President, reflecting the Board's confidence in my leadership, integrity, and commitment to public service. This distinction gives the communities I represent a strong voice in shaping the future of our regional water supply.

During my term, I helped secure more than $90 million in federal and state funding to address toxins known as PFAS, or "forever chemicals," improve groundwater quality, and strengthen water infrastructure.
I remain committed to government accountability, fiscal responsibility, and protecting taxpayers while safeguarding our most valuable natural resource.

Proven experience matters. I respectfully ask for your vote to continue providing experienced, honest leadership while working to ensure a safe, reliable, and affordable groundwater supply for today's families and generations to come.

text: As a Water Policy Analyst and Southeast Los Angeles resident, I am running for the Water Replenishment District to bring new, accountable leadership to our communities.

I am the first in my family to graduate from college. I earned two associate degrees from Long Beach City College before graduating cum laude from the University of Southern California with a bachelor's degree in Political Science, a minor in Communications, Policy, and Law, and a Master of Public Administration.
As Mayor of Bell Gardens, I led and advanced major infrastructure projects, including the opening of our regional aquatic center.
Our communities have been represented by the same person for 20 years, since I was 9 years old. I believe it is time for new leadership.
-Hold data centers accountable so they do not harm our water supply or force families to pay higher costs.
-Protect groundwater through recycling, conservation, stormwater capture, and replenishment.
-Work with cities and fire departments to strengthen water infrastructure and ensure water is available during wildfires and emergencies such as the Lineage warehouse fire.
I respectfully ask for you to vote for me, Jorgel Chavez.
